generated.title: M6.0 Earthquake Strikes Deep Beneath Japan — 352 KM Underground! #shorts
generated.description:
A magnitude 6.0 earthquake struck about 352 km beneath the seafloor off Japan on October 31, 2026 at 22:15 UTC (07:15 on November 1, Japan time), about 58 km south-southeast of Shima, Mie Prefecture, according to the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS).

What USGS reports:
- Magnitude: M6.0 (Mww); the event data has been reviewed by USGS
- Depth: about 352 km (352.4 km), a deep earthquake
- Epicenter: 33.82°N, 136.99°E, offshore south-southeast of Shima
- PAGER alert: green, the lowest level. PAGER is a modeled estimate of potential fatalities and economic losses, not a report of what actually happened
- ShakeMap: strongest estimated shaking intensity III (weak)
- Did You Feel It?: 11 reports as of the USGS update at 22:55 UTC (a count of submitted reports, not of people)
- Tsunami: the USGS record carries no tsunami flag for this earthquake

Why does the depth matter? Most earthquakes begin near the surface. At this depth, earthquakes occur inside tectonic plates that have sunk deep into the mantle. Seismic waves lose energy on the long way up, so deep earthquakes generally produce much weaker shaking at the surface than shallow ones of the same magnitude.

In the information we reviewed, no damage or casualties have been reported. This may change as more information becomes available. Magnitudes are USGS values and may be revised; other agencies, including the Japan Meteorological Agency, can publish different values.

Official event page: https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/eventpage/us7000tuku

Narration is an AI-generated voice (ElevenLabs text-to-speech). The video contains no AI-generated images or footage; the map is drawn from USGS data, Natural Earth and Mapzen terrain.
